[strategy/guidance/application/component-authoring/GUID-APP-COMP-001-component-authoring-guidance.md#executive-summary]

## Executive Summary

This guidance walks a product domain team (or an AI agent acting on their behalf) through the end-to-end process of authoring, validating, and publishing a Portal Studio Product Package.

Each Portal Studio **Module** is a **Webpack 5 Module Federation remote** — a React component exposed via `exposes` in the webpack config and placed on portal pages by Studio Designers. The Portal Studio shell (Next.js) is the MF host; it loads each Module at runtime via `import(remoteEntryUrl)`. React and ReactDOM are shared singletons — declared in the Webpack `shared` config — so they are never bundled into each Module Bundle. Modules also publish an ESM library (`@mmes/{name}`) built with Vite for developer React consumption; these are separate builds.

The mandatory requirements are defined in [STD-APP-COMP-001](../../../standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md). This document is the *how-to* companion — it explains each step with concrete examples so that a domain team or AI agent can produce a compliant package on the first attempt.

**Time estimate:** A first Module with AI tooling takes approximately 1 day (8 hours). Subsequent Modules in the same domain reuse the package scaffold and take 2–4 hours.

## Opt-Out

Portal Studio compliance is **enabled by default** for all repos scaffolded from `eap-bootstrap`. If your repo is a polyglot library with no React/Portal Studio UI (e.g. `mmes-cmn-core`), set `studio_packaging: false` in `.project.yml` to skip all compliance checks. See [STD-APP-COMP-001 § 2.1](../../../standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#21-opt-out-via-projectyml) for details.

For repos with `studio_packaging: true` (the default), continue with the steps below.

[strategy/guidance/application/component-authoring/GUID-APP-COMP-001-component-authoring-guidance.md#prerequisites]

## Prerequisites

Before authoring a Module, confirm:

- [ ] `.project.yml` has `studio_packaging: true` (or key is absent — defaults to true)
- [ ] The domain service's OpenAPI spec is published and accessible
- [ ] The domain team has read [STD-APP-COMP-001](../../../standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md)
- [ ] `mmes-common-core` is available as a dependency (`@mmes/core`)
- [ ] The `studio-package-validator` CLI is installed (`npm install -g @gainwell/studio-package-validator`)
- [ ] JFrog `mmes-npm` access credentials are configured
- [ ] Node.js 20+ and Webpack 5 are available

[strategy/guidance/application/component-authoring/GUID-APP-COMP-001-component-authoring-guidance.md#step-1-scaffold-the-package]

## Step 1: Scaffold the Package

Run the `/ui-component-create` skill or the scaffold tool to generate the package skeleton pre-populated from your domain service's OpenAPI spec:

```bash
npx @gainwell/create-studio-package \
  --domain member \
  --openapi https://member-service.internal/openapi.json \
  --out ./components/react/packages/enrollment
```

This generates:

```
components/react/packages/enrollment/
├── package.json                            ← @mmes/member-enrollment (ESM library)
├── src/modules/MemberSearch/               ← module source
├── studio/
│   ├── package.json                        ← @mmes/member-eligibility-studio-webpack
│   ├── studio-manifest.json                ← pre-populated from OpenAPI (schemaVersion: "1.0")
│   └── webpack.mf.config.js                ← Webpack 5 MF config
└── src/modules/
    └── MemberSearch/
        ├── MemberSearch.tsx
        ├── test/
        │   └── harness.html
        └── tests/
            └── member-member-search.cert.ts
```

If the scaffold tool is not available, create the structure manually following [STD-APP-COMP-001 §3.0](../../../standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#30-package-structure).

[strategy/guidance/application/component-authoring/GUID-APP-COMP-001-component-authoring-guidance.md#step-2-build-the-webpack-5-mf-remote]

## Step 2: Build the Webpack 5 MF Remote

Components are compiled as Webpack 5 Module Federation remotes. Full Webpack configuration requirements are defined in [STD-APP-FE-001 §5.0](../../../standards/application/frontend/STD-APP-FE-001-react-application-standards.md#50-module-federation-standards) — follow those rules exactly. Portal Studio-specific conventions for `webpack.mf.config.cjs`:

- `filename` must be exactly `remoteEntry.js`; output directory must be `dist/mf/`
- `name` must follow `{domain}_{product}` using underscores (e.g. `member_studioWebpack`)
- `exposes` has one entry per component in the package: `'./MemberSearch': './components/member-search/src/MemberSearch'`
- `react`, `react-dom`, and `react-router-dom` must be declared as `shared` singletons — the Portal Studio shell provides them

```bash
webpack --config webpack.mf.config.cjs
# Output: dist/mf/remoteEntry.js + chunks
```

**Bundle size check (gzipped, shared React excluded):**
```bash
gzip -c dist/mf/remoteEntry.js | wc -c
# Must be < 512000 bytes (500 KB)
```

The ESM library build (for developer consumption) remains a separate Vite build per component and is unaffected by this step:
```bash
vite build   # outputs dist/esm/ — independent of the MF remote build
```

[strategy/guidance/application/component-authoring/GUID-APP-COMP-001-component-authoring-guidance.md#step-3-author-the-studio-manifestjson]

## Step 3: Author the studio-manifest.json

Start from the canonical schema at `mmes-common-core/schemas/studio-manifest.v1.schema.json`. A minimal valid manifest (schema v1.0):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://portal-studio.gainwell.com/schemas/studio-manifest.json",
  "schemaVersion": "1.0",
  "product": "member",
  "displayName": "Member",
  "description": "Medicaid member enrollment, eligibility, and coverage management.",
  "version": "1.4.2",
  "publishedAt": "2026-08-11T00:00:00Z",
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "id": "member.search",
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/members",
      "description": "Search members by name or ID",
      "queryParams": ["q", "page", "pageSize"],
      "responseFields": ["id", "name", "dob", "status"]
    }
  ],
  "modules": [
    {
      "namespace": "@member/member-search",
      "version": "1.4.2",
      "displayName": "Member Search",
      "description": "Filter form and results list for finding members.",
      "remoteEntry": "https://gwproductengineering.jfrog.io/@mmes/member-eligibility-studio-webpack/-/remoteEntry.js",
      "exposedModule": "./MemberSearch",
      "packageName": "@mmes/member-eligibility-studio-webpack",
      "certificationTestFile": "tests/member-member-search.cert.ts",
      "a11y": {
        "apgPattern": "combobox",
        "wcagConformance": "AA",
        "notes": "Search input uses combobox; results use aria-live=polite"
      },
      "contract": { },
      "help": { }
    }
  ]
}
```

Fill in the `contract` and `help` blocks in the following steps.

page_texts.9: [strategy/guidance/application/component-authoring/GUID-APP-COMP-001-component-authoring-guidance.md#step-4-declare-typed-properties] ## Step 4: Declare Typed Properties For each component property, declare its type. For values that are locale-sensitive, use the typed property system so Portal Studio applies `@mmes/core/locale_format` formatting automatically. **Standard property (no formatting):** ```json { "name": "placeholder", "type": "string", "description": "Search input placeholder", "default": "Search members..." } ``` **Date property (Portal formats it):** ```json { "name": "service-date", "type": "date", "format": "short", "description": "Service date — formatted by locale_format" } ``` **Currency property (Portal formats it):** ```json { "name": "claim-amount", "type": "currency", "currency": "USD", "description": "Claim amount — formatted by locale_format" } ``` **If any typed properties are `date`, `time`, `datetime`, `currency`, or `number`**, add to the manifest: ```json "platformDependencies": ["@mmes/core/locale_format"] ``` **Component implementation — never format directly:** ```typescript // ❌ Wrong — hardcoded format return {serviceDate.toLocaleDateString('en-US')}; // ✅ Right — receive pre-formatted string from Portal via props return {serviceDate}; // Portal injects the formatted string ``` ---

[strategy/guidance/application/component-authoring/GUID-APP-COMP-001-component-authoring-guidance.md#step-7-declare-accessibility]

## Step 7: Declare Accessibility

Every component must declare its ARIA pattern and WCAG conformance:

```json
"a11y": {
  "apgPattern": "combobox",
  "wcagConformance": "AA",
  "notes": "Search input is a combobox with autocomplete=list. Results use role=listbox with aria-live=polite for dynamic updates. Tab moves through search input → button → first result."
}
```

**Common APG patterns:** `combobox` | `listbox` | `dialog` | `tree` | `grid` | `tabpanel` | `menubar` | `button` | `checkbox` | `radiogroup`

**WCAG AA requirements (non-exhaustive):**
- All interactive elements keyboard accessible
- Focus visible at all times
- Color contrast ratio ≥ 4.5:1 for normal text, ≥ 3:1 for large text
- No information conveyed by color alone
- All images have alt text

[strategy/guidance/application/component-authoring/GUID-APP-COMP-001-component-authoring-guidance.md#step-10-publish-to-jfrog]

## Step 10: Publish to JFrog

```bash
# Set JFrog credentials for @mmes scope
npm config set @mmes:registry https://gwproductengineering.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/npm/mmes-npm/
npm config set //gwproductengineering.jfrog.io/artifactory/api/npm/mmes-npm/:_authToken ${JFROG_TOKEN}

# Publish
npm publish

# Set compliance properties (CI pipeline — use JFrog CLI)
jf rt sp "@mmes/member-eligibility-studio-webpack/-/member-studio-webpack-1.4.2.tgz" \
  "portal.studio.compliant=true;portal.studio.schema.version=1.0;portal.studio.domain=member"
```

**Local development (Verdaccio):**
```bash
npm publish --registry http://localhost:4873
```

[strategy/guidance/application/component-authoring/GUID-APP-COMP-001-component-authoring-guidance.md#common-mistakes]

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Consequence | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `type: "date"` without `format` | Compliance gate rejects | Add `"format": "short"` |
| `type: "currency"` without `currency` | Compliance gate rejects | Add `"currency": "USD"` |
| Formatting dates directly in component | Wrong locale output for es-MX users | Declare typed property, receive pre-formatted string |
| Hardcoded colors in CSS | Dark mode breaks | Use `var(--{product}-color-*, fallback)` (e.g. `var(--member-color-background, #fff)`) |
| `wcagConformance: "A"` | Compliance gate rejects | Minimum is `"AA"` |
| `react` not in `shared` | Duplicate React instances, broken hooks | Add `shared: { react: { singleton: true } }` |
| `remoteEntry` is not an absolute HTTPS URL | Compliance gate rejects | Use full `https://` URL |
| `exposedModule` does not begin with `"./"` | Compliance gate rejects | Use `"./ComponentName"` format |
| `schemaVersion: "1.0""` | Compliance gate rejects | Update manifest to v1.0 schema |
| English text hardcoded in JSX | Not translatable | Move to `contentSlots` |
| No `certificationTestFile` | Compliance gate rejects | Write and declare cert test |
| Publishing without validation | Rejected at import | Run `studio-package-validator` first |
